# Due Diligence

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. A diligence process reduces surprises, it does not eliminate them: findings depend on what the data room actually contains and on the access you are given, and a clean tracker is not a guarantee that a target is sound or that a deal will perform. Curated by Skill Harbor: the due diligence skill of the investment banking pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it the moment a deal moves past a signed letter of intent or a data room opens, on buy-side confirmatory diligence or sell-side vendor diligence, when a vague do-diligence instruction has to become an organized, owner-assigned process. The method runs in eight steps. It frames the scope first (deal type, sector, materiality thresholds, and the investment thesis to prove or disprove), with an explicit warning that an unbounded request list stalls the process, so every ask is anchored to a thesis question. It builds the request list across seven workstreams (commercial, financial, legal, tax, operational, HR and IT), prioritizes quality of earnings inside the financial workstream (revenue recognition, non-recurring items, working-capital trends, normalized EBITDA with a clean add-back bridge, watching for aggressive capitalization or channel stuffing), and covers contracts and change-of-control clauses, litigation, IP ownership, open tax positions, key-person dependencies and IT integration debt across the other streams....
